26.label: Beadle Fuller
26.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

73.label: The Old Examiner's Method
73.desc: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Witnesses keep half again as long before they forget.)

85.label: A Word in the Right Ear
85.desc: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Informers bring word sooner.)

97.desc: The bands have sworn to one shell now, and the shell has a king: Els Vos, the King of Thunes, on a barrel in a cellar under the Warrens. The Vendetta surges every week. Go in Disguise: with the ledger, to break it; with Wit, to parley; with Instinct and Coin, to be tried by its court and stay.

99.label: The King of Thunes: Els Vos
99.desc: Of the Coquille. 6 crimes on the record. The King of Thunes. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's.

105.label: Petition: The Hole
105.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

107.label: Petition: The Rolls
107.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

113.label: Apothecary's Boy Dyer
113.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Sharp: Reads raw proof properly even without the right instrument.

123.label: Informer: Sparrow
123.desc: Kathrin Ebner, known in the taverns as Sparrow. Works The Market. Meet them on the Ward with Coin for a word.

125.label: The Sergeant's Patience
125.desc: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Spent Health, Wit and Instinct come back in half the time.)

133.label: Sworn of a Band: Stoffel Imhoff
133.desc: Sworn of a Band, espieur. 1 crime on the record. Plays at dice every night in a cellar in the Stews. Hurts people. Feeds the Vendetta every week. Has stood before the Blood Court once. Leaves less behind.

149.label: ★ Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row
149.desc: The bucket-chain got there in time to save the walls and nothing else. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. The Carolina says the Fire for whoever did. (The Market) The crier has sung it: the whole city is watching.

152.label: Sworn of a Band: Rafe Dyer
152.desc: Sworn of a Band, planteur. 1 crime on the record. Has pledged the same coat at the Lombard's three times this year. Hurts people. Feeds the Vendetta every week. Has stood before the Blood Court once. Leaves less behind.

156.label: The Ward by Heart
156.desc: Three rounds of the ward, and you notice you no longer look at the doors. You know which are shut and which only look it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Everything in Explore takes a fifth less time.)

163.label: A Tavern Token: the washhouse in Sawyer Row
163.desc: A lead token from the washhouse in Sawyer Row, the kind they give for a drink owed. Rubbed smooth. A chit in a drawer keeps.

164.label: The Message
164.desc: the name of a tavern. This was not the first, and it was not meant to be the last.

166.label: Walburg Sattler
166.desc: Walburg Sattler, the building's owner. Stammers on hard consonants; the whole quarter mimics it. (Accused in: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row)

168.label: Heard on the Round
168.desc: Margery Dyer heard it at the conduit, about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles."

169.label: Rumour from Rattle
169.desc: Rattle heard something about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles."

173.label: Partial: The Hand on the Kindling
173.desc: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn.

175.label: The Vanishing of Walburg Kürschner
175.desc: Walburg Kürschner has not been seen since the night of the storm. the pot was still warm when the neighbour looked in. On the table, an unsent letter. Nobody has asked for a ransom. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Stews)

176.label: Caspar Holzschuher
176.desc: Caspar Holzschuher, a jealous journeyman. Seals letters with a cracked signet: a bird with half a wing. (Accused in: The Vanishing of Walburg Kürschner)

177.label: The Thief-takers' Office
177.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame.

178.label: A Hobnail Scar
178.desc: A deep gouge at the foot of the door, the kind a hobnailed boot makes. A big boot, and a kick.

179.label: Els Vos
179.desc: Els Vos, a known fire-setter. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's. (Accused in: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row)

183.label: Letter: Apothecary's Boy
183.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Costs 3 Coin.

185.label: Sighting: Rafe Dyer
185.desc: Sparrow has seen Rafe Dyer in The Market. Bring this to Rest with their Abroad card to raise the hue and cry. It will not stay true for long.

186.label: A Chit from the washhouse in Sawyer Row
186.desc: Folded small, in the wrong pocket. A chit from the washhouse in Sawyer Row, dated last week. A chit in a drawer keeps.

188.label: A Cracked Seal
188.desc: Wax on the boards by the desk, and in it a bird with half a wing. Not the household's.

189.label: Hans Seiler
189.desc: Hans Seiler, the estranged spouse. Has pledged the same coat at the Lombard's three times this year. (Accused in: The Vanishing of Walburg Kürschner)

192.label: Deposition: Ned Nagel
192.desc: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles." (Wants the reward.)

193.label: Barbel Holzschuher
193.desc: Barbel Holzschuher, a tenant put out. Has ink-black fingers; works a printer's press. (Accused in: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row)

194.label: Blood Court: Stoffel Imhoff
194.desc: Stoffel Imhoff stands before the Blood Court for Hue and Cry: Stoffel Imhoff. The charge looked like full proof.

196.label: The Last Evening
196.desc: the pot was still warm when the neighbour looked in. Whatever happened, it happened fast.

197.label: Rumour from Sparrow
197.desc: Sparrow heard something about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles."

202.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn A0
202.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

204.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn A1
204.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

206.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn A2
206.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

208.label: Band: The Velvet Knives
208.desc: Sworn together by Stoffel Imhoff, Rafe Dyer, Sworn A0, who all walked from you. They feed the Vendetta every week. Post the Watch on them in Attend with a watchman; at Bailiff, go in Disguise to build a case against them.

210.label: Sworn of a Band: Sworn B0
210.desc: Sworn of a Band, crocheteur. 1 crime on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg.

216.label: Band: The Lanternless
216.desc: Sworn together by Sworn A1, Sworn A2, Sworn B0, who all walked from you. They feed the Vendetta every week. Post the Watch on them in Attend with a watchman; at Bailiff, go in Disguise to build a case against them.

journal.title: They Found Each Other
journal.text: Sworn A1, Sworn A2, Sworn B0: every one of them walked away from one of your cases. Now they drink in the same cellar, and call themselves the Lanternless.

journal.title: They Found Each Other
journal.text: Stoffel Imhoff, Rafe Dyer, Sworn A0: every one of them walked away from one of your cases. Now they drink in the same cellar, and call themselves the Velvet Knives.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Word from Sparrow
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row. Sparrow does not sign things.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Walburg Kürschner's Lodging. You find: The Last Evening.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Taken: Stoffel Imhoff
journal.text: The sergeants take them at their shop, in front of everyone. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: The Purse Is Gone
journal.text: Somebody came back for it. They will remember you left it alone. The people who left it remember.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: Ned Nagel talks for an hour. Most of it is about their late husband. Then, almost as an afterthought: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles." They also mention Barbel Holzschuher.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Margery Dyer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Informer's Brother: Send the Watch as planned
journal.text: The brother is taken. Your informer stops meeting your eye. (Standing rises; Vendetta)

journal.title: The Informer's Brother
journal.text: Your informer asks a favour, the first they have ever asked. Their brother runs untaxed wine through the Water-gate. The Watch is due there on Thursday. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Walburg Kürschner's Lodging. You find: A Chit from the washhouse in Sawyer Row, Left Behind: an unsent letter, A Cracked Seal. The first name in the casebook: Hans Seiler. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Stoffel Imhoff, the fugitive. It has to be.

journal.title: A Sighting
journal.text: Sparrow has seen Rafe Dyer. "Same tavern every night. Ask me how I know."

journal.title: An Alibi
journal.text: You try Stoffel Imhoff's story: a bed in the Abbey hospital. It will want checking.

journal.title: Week 10
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. A letter of service lands on your desk: Apothecary's Boy. The ledger: no case closed; 3 open; 2 Coin in hand.

journal.title: An Informer Is Burned
journal.text: Rattle was dragged into an alley and asked who they had been talking to. They survived. They will not be talking to you again.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over a Tenement in Ebner Row. You find: A Hobnail Scar. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Els Vos.

journal.title: The Watch-house: The Thief-takers' Office
journal.text: Masons, lime dust and a blessing from the Bishop's chaplain. The The Thief-takers' Office is open. A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame.

journal.title: New Case: The Vanishing of Walburg Kürschner
journal.text: Walburg Kürschner has not been seen since the night of the storm. the pot was still warm when the neighbour looked in. On the table, an unsent letter. Nobody has asked for a ransom. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn.

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: A Word from Rattle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row. Rattle does not sign things.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at a Tenement in Ebner Row. You find: A Tavern Token: the washhouse in Sawyer Row, The Message, A lit taper dropped carefully. The first name in the casebook: Walburg Sattler.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "The Vanished," says Sparrow, "in The Stews. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Week 9
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. 3 who walked from you are still inside the walls. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: 1 acquittal; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Watchman Dead
journal.text: Clerk Ebner was stabbed on their way home. The burial is on Thursday. The whole Watch-house goes. You carry the coffin.

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: You let Stoffel Imhoff talk about Griet Kramer. Their voice changes when they do. They know you are coming. They have always known.

journal.title: Nothing Doing
journal.text: Rain, cressets, and the ring of pattens on wet stone. Nothing you can use. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: An Insight: The Ward by Heart
journal.text: Three rounds of the ward, and you notice you no longer look at the doors. You know which are shut and which only look it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Margery Dyer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Not Guilty: Rafe Dyer
journal.text: The sworn men acquit. Rafe Dyer walks down the court steps into the crowd's cheering and looks straight at you.

journal.title: Els Vos Again
journal.text: The hand is familiar. The crier's song brings the first of them to your door before the ink is dry. The bucket-chain got there in time to save the walls and nothing else. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. The Carolina says the Fire for whoever did.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at a Bolt-hole in The Harbour. You find: A Loaded Die, Marks on the Sill. The first name in the casebook: Stoffel Imhoff. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: A Knock at Night: Put them up at the Watch-house
journal.text: A bench in the Watch-house and a sergeant who asks no questions. By the week's end nobody is asking after them. (Your informer is safe again)

journal.title: A Knock at Night
journal.text: Your informer is on your stair at midnight with a bag. Somebody has been asking after them by name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: Taken: Rafe Dyer
journal.text: The sergeants take them at their shop, in front of everyone. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. The ledger: 1 acquittal; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Which Stair Is Yours
journal.text: A man has been asking in the Red Ox which stair is yours. He was not asking for the landlord.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Sighting
journal.text: Rattle leans in. "Stoffel Imhoff. I know where they sleep."

journal.title: Sighting: Stoffel Imhoff
journal.text: Rattle has seen Stoffel Imhoff. Stoffel Imhoff has been seen again. They walked once. The trail is warm, for now.

journal.title: Delivered: The Apothecary's Key
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: Not Guilty: Stoffel Imhoff
journal.text: The Council wanted this answered. It was not. The sworn men acquit. Stoffel Imhoff walks down the court steps into the crowd's cheering and looks straight at you.

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Break it up
journal.text: Two carters in the cells and a tapster who remembers who kept his window. He pays in silver. (+2 Coin from a grateful tapster)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Hal Fuller walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Rafe Dyer, a goldsmith's journeyman. It has to be.

journal.title: An Insight: The Sergeant's Patience
journal.text: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: A New Contact
journal.text: You pull someone out of a brawl in The Market. They owe you now. They call themselves Sparrow. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: The Rival Exposed
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. The Council reads the file in silence and sends the Harbourmaster's Examiner back to the Customs House. Your name is spoken in the chamber, warmly for once.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The apothecary's acid finds lead under the silver, and the same flaw in the Emperor's eye on every piece. One die.

journal.title: Taken: Stoffel Imhoff
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Week 7
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Neeltje Ebner takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Reads a ledger like a romance and a forged hand like a confession. Ink under every nail.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Cattle Market. You find: The Bad Coin. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Dorcas Kuiper. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Margery Dyer takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: You swear the oath in the Council chamber with your hand on the Carolina, and the clerk writes your name under the last Examiner's, which has a line through it. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Stoffel Imhoff, the night-clerk. It has to be.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Cattle Market. You find: The Light Scale, A twist of clippings, A Lombard's Chit. The first name in the casebook: Rafe Dyer. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Weakness Found
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. They will be careful for a week. One more, and you will have them.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Els Vos has done it again. The Watch-house will hear of it when a desk is clear. Piet Wieland has taken up one of your cases. A letter of service lands on your desk: Clerk. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 9 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Rival Takes a Case
journal.text: Piet Wieland is working Fire at the Webster Print-shop from the other side, with the Harbourmaster's men. Answer it first, or they will.

journal.title: The Coquille
journal.text: You have seen the same advocate at every hearing, the same faces at every cellar door. Behind the city's crime there is a court, a barrel for a throne, and a king. They call it the Coquille. Go in Disguise to get at its books. The name is Els Vos. It is not in your Rolls. It will be.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Rattle counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about False Coin in the Cattle Market.

journal.title: Marked: Rattle
journal.text: Somebody in the Warrens has asked, by name, who Rattle's friend at the Watch-house is. They stop coming to the bench. Guard them in Attend with a watchman, or the next time they are asked it will not be politely.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about False Coin in the Cattle Market.

journal.title: New Case: False Coin in the Cattle Market
journal.text: The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in the Cattle Market for a year: shavings in the sweepings. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a twist of clippings. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Flogging and Banishment: Barbel Molenaar
journal.text: Barbel Molenaar is whipped at the cart's tail to the Harbour gate and forbidden the city for ten years. The gate shuts. Some of them come back.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Rattle counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Fire at the Webster Print-shop.

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Barbel Molenaar
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Barbel Molenaar is convicted of Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Trijn Claesz presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.title: Condemned: Barbel Molenaar
journal.text: Barbel Molenaar goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea, A Family's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Rattle counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Fire at the Webster Print-shop.

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk: Pocket it
journal.text: Silver is silver. Somebody now believes you can be bought, because you can. (+3 Coin; the Council's eye)

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk
journal.text: Nobody saw who left it. Three Coin, good silver, and a note with the name of a case on it and nothing else. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Webster Print-shop. You find: The Message. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Moll Tucher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: An Evening Off
journal.text: You walk to the mill-race and back without once thinking about a case. On the way home you think about one. It is a start.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Piet Wieland has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Coining," says Rattle, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close.

journal.title: Taken: Barbel Molenaar
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Stress
journal.text: You wake at the same hour every night with the same case behind your eyes. You have started to snap at the sergeant. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Webster Print-shop. You find: The Smell Under the Smoke, A rag pushed under the door, A Loaded Die. The first name in the casebook: Stoffel Imhoff.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Barbel Molenaar, a receiver from the Market. It has to be.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Small Kindness
journal.text: You catch a cutpurse at the corner of the Market. The stallholder presses coin into your hand and will not take it back. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: Fire at the Webster Print-shop
journal.text: Somebody set fire to the Webster Print-shop while the family slept upstairs. It started with a rag pushed under the door. The message came the next morning: the name of a tavern. The Council wants it answered within 18 days, and would take it kindly if Aeltje Cooper, of a Council family, were not the name.

journal.title: The Confessor: Leave the seal alone
journal.text: He is grateful, and says so where the Bishop can hear it. (The Bishop's favour)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Word from Rattle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's. Rattle does not sign things.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: the Tiler talks for an hour. Most of it is about their late husband. Then, almost as an afterthought: "A shell on the hat, like the pilgrims."

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Kramer the Goldsmith's. You find: A Shell on the Sill. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Bartel de Groot. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Hal Fuller walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. A great deal of it. The barber-surgeon in the Abbey Close stitched a hand the same morning. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Kramer the Goldsmith's. You find: Blood on the Glass. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Barbel Molenaar. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Word from Rattle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's. Rattle does not sign things.

journal.title: The Day-book
journal.text: Forty people come to the desk. Thirty-nine of them are nothing.

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother: Give him the week, and his wage
journal.text: He goes. The others see it. (Standing rises; Dread eases)

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother
journal.text: One of your watchmen asks for the week: his mother is dying in the Warrens and there is nobody else. The round will be short a man. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Hal Fuller takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Word from Rattle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's. Rattle does not sign things.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Kramer the Goldsmith's. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Endres Bader. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Carolina
journal.text: They gave you the Emperor's law with the letter: two witnesses, or a confession, or nothing. You have read it. You know exactly which pages you will tear out, and in what order. First, the burglary on the desk.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's
journal.text: Splinters everywhere at Trijn Claesz's. Someone went through the shop window, with a cobble at the dead of the night, took whatever stood in the shop front, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing a cart with the tail-board up.

history.title: False Coin in the Cattle Market
